title: Mark Wahlberg on using AI in film ‘the right way’ and being open to an AI clone carrying on his legacy
slides: What if Mark Wahlberg's legacy outlives him as an AI clone?
He says AI in film must be used 'the right way'
He's open to a digital clone continuing his work
Actors could license their likeness instead of losing it
Ask: who controls your face after you stop?
thread_text:
1. Legacy or likeness?

Mark Wahlberg says he's open to a digital clone continuing his work after he's gone. That's not a sci-fi pitch — it's a contract question.

2. The right way

Wahlberg insists AI in film must be used 'the right way.' The problem: nobody has defined what that means, and studios are already drafting the terms.

3. License, don't lose

Actors could license their likeness instead of signing it away. That flips the power dynamic — but only if the contract gives them veto power over new roles.

4. Who controls your face?

After you stop, your digital clone could still be auditioning. Wahlberg's idea raises a question every actor will face: who owns your face when you're not there to say no?

5. Check your contract

Open your last release form and search for 'likeness' and 'AI.' If those words aren't there, you've already given away more than you think.
